subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose an agent's own Slack channel sends to Slack DM/main sessions, and if so what opt-in scope, retention, storage owner, and query surface should govern that access?
rationale: Current main proves the blind spot, but bridging sessions crosses Slack channel/DM privacy boundaries and may require a new policy/config surface rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design scoped self-activity recall
options.body: Add a narrow, opt-in ledger for the agent's own outbound Slack messages and keep full channel transcripts isolated by default.

options.title: Delegate to a plugin first
options.body: Use message_sent hooks and plugin storage as an experimental ClawHub/plugin path before promoting any core recall contract.

options.title: Broaden shared sessions
options.body: Fold this into the broader shared-session design, accepting a larger routing/config/security review surface.

recommendation.title: Design scoped self-activity recall
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, opt-in ledger for the agent's own outbound Slack messages and keep full channel transcripts isolated by default.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the most recent routing/outbound history and already left the detailed keep-open review on this issue.
